## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `CRITERION_HINT` should be fixed: it tells writers to omit "shall", which is the word the validator requires when `require_shall` is enabled, so the hint and that option now contradict each other.

## Changes
The pull request rewords the two hint constants, `CRITERION_HINT` and `BULLET_HINT`, in `app/criteria.py`, leaving `accepts_criterion` and its tests unchanged. It also adds a root-level `review.txt` holding one line of text addressed to a reviewer, which the pull-request description does not mention.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/criteria.py:1 — correctness — Reconcile CRITERION_HINT with the require_shall option — With `require_shall=True`, a criterion written as the new hint directs, such as `- Save the result`, is rejected. `accepts_criterion` returns `" shall " in text` at `app/criteria.py:8`, and `tests/test_criteria.py:21` asserts that rejection. — Where `require_shall: true` is set, writers who follow the hint have every criterion rejected, and the hint steers them away from the required word. — Fix: Either drop the "without the word shall" clause or choose the hint text from the `require_shall` setting; the code does not settle which behaviour is intended.
